SPCH 140.description: Introduction to theory and practice of oral communication in public, social, and institutional contexts. Includes foundational and cumulative training in the invention, performance, and critical analysis of oral communication, with emphasis on argumentation, persuasion, audience analysis, delivery, and ethical forms of engagement.
SPCH 140.subject: SPCH
SPCH 140.title: Public Communication

SPCH 145.description: Introduction to theory and practice of live and recorded online spoken communication in public, social, and institutional contexts. Training in invention, performance, and critical analysis of online spoken communication, including audience analysis, persuasion, delivery, and ethical engagement. Includes significant practice in preparing and presenting live online public communication.
SPCH 145.subject: SPCH
SPCH 145.title: Online Public Communication

SPCH 150.description: Exercises and techniques to reduce and manage public speaking anxiety. Ideally taken concurrently with any course that requires multiple presentations.
SPCH 150.subject: SPCH
SPCH 150.title: Public Speaking Anxiety Reduction

SPCH 201.description: Examination of historical and popular communication conflicts, texts, and events. Offers an introduction to critical concepts and analysis of public speech, rhetoric, and cultural discourse.
SPCH 201.subject: SPCH
SPCH 201.title: Popular Communication and Public Culture

SPCH 213.description: Moral issues confronting men and women in contemporary society and the challenges of communicating effectively about them. Topics will vary but may include access to health care, euthanasia, abortion, same sex marriage and the moral and environmental consequences of eating animals.
SPCH 213.subject: SPCH
SPCH 213.title: Communicating Moral Issues

SPCH 230.description: Fundamentals of oral communication within business and professional settings. Includes performance.
SPCH 230.subject: SPCH
SPCH 230.title: Business and Professional Speaking

SPCH 260.description: Preparing and delivering the debate. Academic debate serves as a model.
SPCH 260.subject: SPCH
SPCH 260.title: Argumentation and Debate

SPCH 330.description: The development of the skills and methods of effective participation in teams, committees, and other small groups.
SPCH 330.subject: SPCH
SPCH 330.title: Small Group Communication

SPCH 331.description: Examines communication behavior and networks within organizations through the study of major theories of organizational communication, identifies and defines primary concepts, and applies them to organizational scenarios and case studies.
SPCH 331.subject: SPCH
SPCH 331.title: Organizational Communication

SPCH 340.description: Introduction to the study of literature through performance; reading, analysis, and performance of prose, poetry, nonfiction, and drama.
SPCH 340.subject: SPCH
SPCH 340.title: Literature and Performance

SPCH 380.description: Analysis of the process and functions of persuasive communication.
SPCH 380.subject: SPCH
SPCH 380.title: Persuasive Communication

SPCH 387.description: Theories of human communication useful for understanding and informing the everyday work of writers. Emphasis on intensive analysis and writing.
SPCH 387.subject: SPCH
SPCH 387.title: Introduction to Rhetoric

SPCH 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
SPCH 399.subject: SPCH
SPCH 399.title: Independent Study and Research

SPCH 411.description: The study of texts and discourse from contemporary culture drawing from concepts such as politics, television, music, and other popular culture and entertainment.
SPCH 411.subject: SPCH
SPCH 411.title: Arguments in Cultural Studies

SPCH 441.description: Interpretation and evaluation of communication texts and events such as speeches, media, and social movements. Employs a variety of critical methods and approaches.
SPCH 441.subject: SPCH
SPCH 441.title: Rhetorical Criticism

SPCH 448.description: Analysis and evaluation of speeches, political campaigns and controversies over political representation and recognition. Focus on case studies that illustrate the role of speech-making in political campaigns. Offered only in fall semesters in which national elections are held.
SPCH 448.subject: SPCH
SPCH 448.title: Contemporary Political Rhetoric

SPCH 463.description: A study of debates at the Constitutional Convention, Lincoln-Douglas debates (1858), vice presidential and presidential debates, and other national debates.
SPCH 463.subject: SPCH
SPCH 463.title: Great Debates

SPCH 464.description: An exploration of the process of advanced policy advocacy emphasizing speechwriting strategies, issues management, and systematic advocacy campaigns.
SPCH 464.subject: SPCH
SPCH 464.title: Speechwriting

SPCH 470.description: Rhetorical study of science and technology in contemporary culture, emphasizing the ways scientific texts and technologies make their persuasive appeals.
SPCH 470.subject: SPCH
SPCH 470.title: Rhetoric of Science and Technology

SPCH 471.description: Classical rhetoric and its ongoing influence in the modern world, emphasizing how the study and use of language in ancient Greece and Rome continue to shape modern communication.
SPCH 471.subject: SPCH
SPCH 471.title: Rhetoric and the Ancient Roots of Modern Life

SPCH 472.description: Rhetorical study of popular culture, using the methods and theories of cultural analysis to examine how various popular cultural forms work as persuasion.
SPCH 472.subject: SPCH
SPCH 472.title: Rhetoric and Popular Culture

SPCH 485.description: Study of rhetoric by and about women as manifested in speeches, essays, and other rhetorical artifacts.
SPCH 485.subject: SPCH
SPCH 485.title: Women’s Rhetoric

SPCH 486.description: African-American rhetoric as manifested in speeches, essays, and other rhetorical artifacts.
SPCH 486.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: WGST 111 or WGST 112 or ANTH 102.
SPCH 486.subject: SPCH
SPCH 486.title: African-American Rhetoric

SPCH 499.description: Reading and research on selected topics. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. May be repeated once as topics vary.
SPCH 499.subject: SPCH
SPCH 499.title: Special Topics in Speech

SPCH 543.description: Examines the role of communication in legal and judicial contexts. Focus on case studies that illustrate the theoretical and practical significance of rhetoric in the work of the courts, lawyers, and public advocacy groups.
SPCH 543.subject: SPCH
SPCH 543.title: Communication, Law, and Society

SPCH 700.description: Introduction to theories, concepts, and analysis in critical rhetorical and communication research. Emphasis on rhetoric, public advocacy and discourse, performance, critical theory.
SPCH 700.subject: SPCH
SPCH 700.title: Introduction to the Advanced Study of Speech Communication Rhetoric

SPCH 701.description: Survey of issues, theories, and methods of pedagogy in speech communication, rhetoric, and performance studies.
SPCH 701.subject: SPCH
SPCH 701.title: Pedagogies of Speech Communication Rhetoric

SPCH 734.description: Advanced study of theories and practices of public and cultural argumentation. Emphasis on critical argumentation theories and analysis of public arguments.
SPCH 734.subject: SPCH
SPCH 734.title: Theories of Public Argumentation

SPCH 736.description: Examination of the role of language, rhetoric, and argumentation in the historical and contemporary project of critical social theory.
SPCH 736.subject: SPCH
SPCH 736.title: Critical Theory Rhetoric

SPCH 741.description: Advanced study of theories of rhetorical criticism and the conceptual assumptions that motivate, compose, and justify critical interpretations of rhetorical acts, performances, and events.
SPCH 741.subject: SPCH
SPCH 741.title: Theory and Practice of Rhetorical Criticism

SPCH 744.description: Examination of the rhetorical operations that define, sustain, and reshape historical and contemporary forms of civil society, including modes of public address, community engagement, non-profit advocacy, and political communication.
SPCH 744.subject: SPCH
SPCH 744.title: Public Advocacy and Civil Society

SPCH 746.description: Advanced study of the rhetoric of political social movements.
SPCH 746.subject: SPCH
SPCH 746.title: Rhetoric of Movements

SPCH 747.description: Advanced study of institutional discourse and the role of institutional argumentation in the formation and critique of power. Includes directed inquiry into the rhetorical dynamics of consensus-formation, dissent, and recognition as they unfold between institutions, publics, and cultures.
SPCH 747.subject: SPCH
SPCH 747.title: Rhetorical Power, Institutional Discourse, and Recognition

SPCH 749.description: Theories and research exploring the mutual contributions of performance and cultural studies. Emphasis on performance as both a subject of critical/cultural inquiry as well as a method of critical/cultural invention.
SPCH 749.subject: SPCH
SPCH 749.title: Performance and Cultural Studies

SPCH 751.description: Study of critical performance methods and the conceptual and paradigmatic assumptions that motivate, compose, and justify performance as a critical act, criticism as a performative act, and performance events as critical objects.
SPCH 751.subject: SPCH
SPCH 751.title: Performance Criticism

SPCH 755.description: Exploration of performance as a site of and means for representing and creating social change.
SPCH 755.subject: SPCH
SPCH 755.title: Theories of Performance, Representation, and Advocacy

SPCH 761.description: Examination of the ethical and political commitments in the rhetorical tradition. Emphasis on the intersection of rhetorical scholarship with issues in communication ethics and their implications for political rhetoric.
SPCH 761.subject: SPCH
SPCH 761.title: Ethics Politics of Rhetoric

SPCH 762.description: Study of the rhetorical analysis of scientific and technological public discourse, implications of public science and technological changes for the theory and practice of rhetoric, and the rhetorical construction of sciences and technologies.
SPCH 762.subject: SPCH
SPCH 762.title: Rhetorics of Materiality, Technology, and Science

SPCH 764.description: Advanced study of the rhetorical violence that attends the human condition and its attempted redress through discourses of human rights. Special attention devoted to theories of violence and critical interpretation of legal discourse, human rights doctrine, and humanitarian advocacy.
SPCH 764.subject: SPCH
SPCH 764.title: Rhetoric, Violence, and the Discourse of Human Rights

SPCH 790.description: Selected topics in speech communication. rhetoric, and performance studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
SPCH 790.subject: SPCH
SPCH 790.title: Special Topics in Speech Communication, Rhetoric, and Performance

SPCH 792.description: Survey of ancient Greek and Roman rhetorical theory. Non-degree students may not enroll without the consent of the Director of Graduate Studies in English.
SPCH 792.subject: SPCH
SPCH 792.title: Classical Rhetoric

SPCH 793.description: Survey of major theories of rhetoric from medieval to modern times. Non-degree students may not enroll without the consent of the Director of Graduate Studies in English.
SPCH 793.subject: SPCH
SPCH 793.title: Rhetorical Theory and Practice, Medieval to Modern

SPCH 794.description: Survey of 20th-century contributions to rhetorical theory. Non-degree students may not enroll without the consent of the Director of Graduate Studies in English.
SPCH 794.subject: SPCH
SPCH 794.title: Modern Rhetorical Theory

SPCH 796.description: Individually arranged studies in specialized areas of speech communication, rhetoric, or performance.
SPCH 796.subject: SPCH
SPCH 796.title: Independent Study in Speech Communication, Rhetoric, and Performance

SPCH 797.description: Individually research projects focused on a selected area of speech communication, rhetoric, or performance.
SPCH 797.subject: SPCH
SPCH 797.title: Special Projects in Speech Communication, Rhetoric, and Performance

SPCH 799.description: To be arranged by candidates for the Master of Arts degree with the instructor under whose direction the master's thesis is being written.
SPCH 799.subject: SPCH
SPCH 799.title: Thesis Preparation
